title.zh: 卷七十三 唐書49: 列傳25 毛璋 聶嶼 溫韜 段凝 孔謙 李鄴
title.en: Volume 73 Book of Later Tang 49: Biographies 25 - Mao Zhang, Nie Yu, Wen Tao, Duan Ning, Kong Qian, Li Ye
title.raw: 卷七十三 唐書49: 列傳25 毛璋 聶嶼 溫韜 段凝 孔謙 李鄴 Volume 73 Book of Later Tang 49: Biographies 25 - Mao Zhang, Nie Yu, Wen Tao, Duan Ning, Kong Qian, Li Ye

sentences.zh: 毛璋，本滄州小校。

translations.literal: Mao Zhang was originally a petty officer in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zhang began as a low-ranking soldier in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁將戴思遠帥滄州，時莊宗已定魏博，思遠勢蹙，棄州遁去，璋據城歸莊宗，

translations.literal: When Liang general Dai Siyuan commanded Cangzhou, Zhuangzong had already secured Weibo; Dai was pressed hard, abandoned the prefecture and fled, and Zhang held the city and submitted to Zhuangzong,
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang general Dai Siyuan held Cangzhou, Zhuangzong had already pacified Weibo. Dai found himself cornered, abandoned the prefecture and fled, and Zhang seized the city and submitted to Zhuangzong,

sentences.zh: （《玉堂閑話》：戴思遠任浮陽日，有部曲毛璋，為性輕悍。

translations.literal: (Idle Talk of the Jade Hall: When Dai Siyuan held Fuyang, he had a soldier under his command named Mao Zhang, who was by nature impulsive and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: (From Idle Talk of the Jade Hall: While Dai Siyuan was stationed at Fuyang, one of his troops was Mao Zhang, a man of reckless and violent temperament.

sentences.zh: 嘗與數十卒追捕盜賊，還宿於逆旅，毛枕劍而寢。

translations.literal: Once, pursuing bandits with several dozen soldiers, they lodged at an inn on the return journey; Mao slept with his sword as a pillow.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he pursued bandits with several dozen men; on the way back they stayed at a roadside inn, and Mao slept with his sword beneath his head.

sentences.zh: 夜分，其劍忽大吼，躍出鞘外，從卒聞者愕然驚異，毛亦神之。

translations.literal: At midnight his sword suddenly roared loudly and leaped out of its scabbard; the soldiers who heard it were startled and amazed, and Mao himself regarded it as supernatural.
translations.idiomatic: Around midnight the sword suddenly gave a great roar and sprang from its scabbard. The men with him were dumbfounded, and Mao himself took it as an omen.

sentences.zh: 乃持劍祝曰：「某若異日有此山河，爾當更鳴躍，否則已。

translations.literal: He then took up the sword and prayed: "If I am someday to possess these mountains and rivers, you shall roar and leap again; otherwise, cease."
translations.idiomatic: He raised the sword and prayed: "If I am one day to hold these mountains and rivers, you shall roar and leap again; if not, be still."

sentences.zh: 」毛復寢，未熟，劍吼躍如初，毛深自負。

translations.literal: " Mao slept again; before he had fallen fully asleep the sword roared and leaped as before, and Mao took great pride in this.
translations.idiomatic: " He lay down once more; before sleep had deepened the sword roared and leaped as before, and Mao was filled with self-assurance.

sentences.zh: 其後戴離鎮，毛請留，戴從之。

translations.literal: Later, when Dai left his post, Mao asked to remain behind and Dai consented.
translations.idiomatic: When Dai later left his command, Mao asked to stay behind and Dai agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，毛以州歸命於唐莊宗，莊宗以毛為其州刺史，後竟帥滄海。）〉

translations.literal: Before long Mao surrendered the prefecture to Tang Zhuangzong; Zhuangzong made Mao prefect of Qizhou, and Mao eventually became military commissioner of Canghai.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Before long Mao turned the prefecture over to Tang Zhuangzong, who appointed him prefect of Qizhou; in the end he came to command Canghai as military commissioner.)〉

sentences.zh: 曆貝州、遼州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Beizhou and Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Beizhou and Liaozhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 璋性凶悖，有膽略，從征河上，屢有戰功。

translations.literal: Zhang was brutal and overbearing, bold and resourceful; campaigning on the Yellow River front he won repeated battle honors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was savage and defiant, with courage and stratagem; on the river campaigns he won merit again and again.

sentences.zh: 梁平，授滄州節度使。

translations.literal: When the Liang fell, he was appointed military commissioner of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang was overthrown, he was made military commissioner of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王師討蜀，以璋為行營右廂馬軍都指揮使；

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, he was made commander of the right wing of the campaigning army's cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: When the court marched against Shu, he was appointed commander of the campaigning army's right-wing cavalry;

sentences.zh: 蜀平，璋功居多。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, Zhang's merits were among the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified, his contribution ranked among the foremost.

sentences.zh: 明年，蕭牆禍起，繼岌自西川至渭南，部下散亡，其川貨妓樂，為璋所掠。

translations.literal: The next year the disaster within the palace walls erupted; Li Jiji came from western Shu to Weinan, his followers scattered, and the Sichuan wealth and entertainers were plundered by Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year palace intrigue broke out. Li Jiji came down from western Shu to Weinan while his followers scattered; the Sichuan goods and entertainers were seized by Zhang.

sentences.zh: 明宗嗣位，錄平蜀功，授邠州節度使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong succeeded, Zhang's merit in pacifying Shu was recognized and he was made military commissioner of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, his service in pacifying Shu was recorded and he was appointed military commissioner of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 璋既家富於財，有蜀之妓樂，驕僭自大，動多不法，招致部下，繕理兵仗。

translations.literal: Now wealthy from his loot, with Shu entertainers, he grew arrogant and extravagant, constantly violating the law, gathering followers, and stockpiling weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Once his household was rich with plunder and he possessed Shu entertainers, he grew arrogant and overbearing, broke the law at every turn, gathered followers, and readied arms.

sentences.zh: 朝廷移授昭義節度使，璋謀欲不奉詔，判官邊蔚密言規責，乃僶勉承命。

translations.literal: The court reassigned him as military commissioner of Zhaoyi; Zhang plotted to refuse the order, but his aide Bian Wei privately admonished him, and he reluctantly accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court transferred him to Zhaoyi as military commissioner. Zhang plotted to defy the edict, until his aide Bian Wei secretly rebuked him and he grudgingly obeyed.

sentences.zh: 洎至潞州，狂妄不悛，每擁川妓於山亭院，服赭黃，縱酒，令為王衍在蜀之戲。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Luzhou he did not mend his ways; each day he surrounded himself with Sichuan entertainers in the mountain pavilion courtyard, wore yellow robes reserved for emperors, drank freely, and had them perform the plays Wang Yan had staged in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Luzhou he did not reform. Day after day he kept Sichuan entertainers in the mountain-pavilion courtyard, dressed in imperial yellow, drank without restraint, and had them perform the same plays Wang Yan had put on in Shu.

sentences.zh: 事聞於朝，征為金吾上將軍。

translations.literal: When news reached court, he was summoned as General of the Golden Insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the court, and he was recalled to serve as General of the Golden Insignia.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，東川節度使董璋上言：「毛璋男廷贇齎父書往西川，慮有陰事。

translations.literal: That autumn the eastern Sichuan military commissioner Dong Zhang reported: "Mao Zhang's son Yan Yun is carrying his father's letter west to Sichuan, and there is reason to fear secret designs."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the eastern Sichuan commissioner Dong Zhang memorialized: "Mao Zhang's son Yan Yun is taking his father's letter to western Shu, and one must fear some hidden plot."

sentences.zh: 」因追廷贇及同行人趙延祚，與璋俱下御史台獄。

translations.literal: Yan Yun and his traveling companion Zhao Yanzuo were pursued and arrested, and Zhang too was committed to the Censorate prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yun and his companion Zhao Yanzuo were pursued and seized, and Zhang was also sent down to the Censorate prison.

sentences.zh: 廷贇乃璋之假侄，稱有叔在蜀，欲往省之，亦無私書，詔停任，令歸私第。

translations.literal: Yan Yun was Zhang's fictive nephew and said he had an uncle in Shu and wished to visit him; there was no private letter. An edict halted proceedings and allowed him to return to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yun was Zhang's adopted nephew and said only that he had an uncle in Shu whom he wished to visit; there was no secret letter. An edict suspended the case and let him return home.

sentences.zh: 初，延祚在獄，多言璋陰事，璋許重賂，以塞其口。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhao Yanzuo in prison had spoken much of Zhang's secret affairs; Zhang had promised him a heavy bribe to silence him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Zhao Yanzuo was in prison, he had disclosed much of Zhang's hidden conduct. Zhang promised him a large bribe to keep silent.

sentences.zh: 及免，延祚征其賂，璋拒而不與，以至延祚詣台訴璋翻覆，復下御史台訊鞫。

translations.literal: When released Yanzuo demanded payment but Zhang refused, so Yanzuo went to the censorate accusing Zhang of bad faith, and Zhang was interrogated again.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanzuo was released he demanded the payment; Zhang refused, and Yanzuo went to the censorate to accuse him of going back on his word. Zhang was interrogated once more.

sentences.zh: 中丞呂夢奇以璋前蒙昭雪，今延祚以責賂之故，復加織羅，故稍佑璋。

translations.literal: Vice censor Lü Mengqi, since Zhang had been cleared before and Yanzuo now charged bribe default, was weaving further charges, so he somewhat favored Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor Lü Mengqi, seeing that Zhang had already been cleared once and that Yanzuo now pressed a claim over an unpaid bribe, was piling on new charges and therefore leaned somewhat in Zhang's favor.

sentences.zh: 及款狀上聞，或云夢奇受璋賂，所以獄不盡情，執之，移於軍巡。

translations.literal: When the confession reached the throne, some said Mengqi had taken a bribe from Zhang so the case was not fully pursued; he was arrested and the case transferred to Military Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the written confession reached the throne, some said Mengqi had accepted a bribe from Zhang and therefore had not pressed the case to the full. Mengqi was arrested and the matter moved to Military Circuit.

sentences.zh: 璋具狀曾許延祚賂未與，又云曾借馬與夢奇，別無行賂之事。

translations.literal: Zhang's full confession admitted he had once promised Yanzuo a bribe but not paid, and also that he had lent a horse to Mengqi, with no other bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's full statement admitted that he had promised Yanzuo a bribe but never paid it, and that he had once lent Mengqi a horse, but denied any other bribery.

sentences.zh: 朝廷懲其宿惡，長流儒州，賜死於路。

translations.literal: The court punished his long-standing wickedness by banishing him to Ruzhou and ordering death en route.
translations.idiomatic: The court punished his long accumulation of evil by banishing him to Ruzhou and ordering him put to death on the way.

sentences.zh: 聶嶼，鄴中人。

translations.literal: Nie Yu was a native of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Yu came from Ye.

sentences.zh: 少為僧，漸學吟詠。

translations.literal: In youth he became a monk and gradually learned poetry.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he became a monk and gradually learned to compose verse.

sentences.zh: 鄭玨之再主禮闈也，與鄉人趙都俱赴鄉薦，都納賄於玨，人報翌日登第，嶼聞不捷，詬來人以嚇之，玨懼，俾俱成名。

translations.literal: When Zheng Jue again presided over the metropolitan examination, he and fellow townsman Zhao Du both went for the provincial test; Du paid a bribe to Jue, and people reported Du would rank the next day. When Yu heard he had failed, he cursed the messenger to frighten them; Jue feared this and arranged for both to pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Jue again ran the metropolitan examinations, Yu and his fellow townsman Zhao Du both sat for the provincial test. Du paid Jue a bribe, and word went about that Du would place the next day. Hearing that he himself had failed, Yu cursed the messenger to scare them. Jue was alarmed and saw to it that both men passed.

sentences.zh: 漸為拾遺，依郭崇韜為鎮州書記。

translations.literal: He gradually rose to Reminder of the Left, serving Guo Chongtao as secretary at Zhen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by degrees to Reminder of the Left and served Guo Chongtao as secretary at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，為起居舍人。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong he was Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he became Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 雙眸若懸，性氣乖僻，人多忌之。

translations.literal: His two eyes seemed to hang forward, his temperament perverse; many resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His eyes bulged as if hanging forward, and his disposition was contrary; many came to dislike him.

sentences.zh: 天成初，除鄴都留守判官，與趙敬怡、呂夢奇不足。

translations.literal: Early in Tiancheng he became aide to the Ye garrison commandant and was on bad terms with Zhao Jingyi and Lü Mengqi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was made aide to the Ye garrison commandant and fell out with Zhao Jingyi and Lü Mengqi.

sentences.zh: 又改河東節度，及至，常鄙其土風，薄其人士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hedong prefecture; upon arrival he constantly despised local customs and belittled local gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Hedong. Once there, he constantly looked down on local customs and slighted local men of standing.

sentences.zh: 或達於重誨，會敬怡入為樞密使，與夢奇同構殺之。

translations.literal: This reached Zhu Hongli; when Jingyi became Military Affairs Commissioner he plotted with Mengqi to kill Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Word of this reached Zhu Hongli. When Jingyi entered office as Military Affairs Commissioner, he joined Mengqi in a plot to kill Yu.

sentences.zh: 嶼早依郭崇韜門庭，致身朱紫，名登兩史，浙江使回，生涯巨萬。

translations.literal: Yu had long relied on Guo Chongtao's patronage, rose to scarlet and purple rank, and his name entered both histories; returning from Zhejiang as envoy, his estate was immense.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had long clung to Guo Chongtao's patronage, rose to the highest court ranks, and had his name entered in both histories. After returning from service as envoy to Zhejiang, his household wealth was enormous.

sentences.zh: 嶼內河東節判時，郭氏次子之婦，孀居於家，嶼喪偶未久，復忍而納幣，人皆罪之。

translations.literal: While Yu was Hedong judge, Guo's younger son's wife was widowed at home; Yu had not long been bereaved of his wife yet still took her as bride—a thing all condemned.
translations.idiomatic: While Yu was judge at Hedong, the younger son of the Guo household had a widowed daughter-in-law living at home. Yu had not long lost his own wife, yet he still sent betrothal gifts to her, and all judged him harshly.

sentences.zh: 明宗在藩邸時，素聞其醜聲。

translations.literal: Mingzong in his princely residence had long heard of his ugly reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Mingzong was still in his princely residence, he had long heard of Yu's foul repute.

sentences.zh: 天成中，與溫韜等同詔賜死。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng, he was granted death along with Wen Tao and others by edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era he was ordered to die by edict, together with Wen Tao and others.

sentences.zh: 溫韜，華原人。

translations.literal: Wen Tao was a native of Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tao came from Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 少為盜，據華原，事李茂貞，名彥韜，後降於梁，更名昭圖。

translations.literal: In youth a bandit, he seized Huayuan and served Li Maozhen, named Yan Tao; later he surrendered to Liang and changed his name to Zhaotu.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was a bandit who seized Huayuan and served Li Maozhen under the name Yan Tao. Later he surrendered to Liang and was renamed Zhaotu.

sentences.zh: 為耀州節度，唐諸陵在境者悉發之，取所藏金寶：而昭陵最固，悉藏前世圖書，鍾、王紙墨，筆跡如新。

translations.literal: As military commissioner of Yaozhou he excavated all Tang tombs in his jurisdiction and took the buried treasure; Zhaoling was most secure, holding books of past ages, Zhong and Wang calligraphy, with brush traces like new.
translations.idiomatic: As commissioner of Yaozhou he opened every Tang imperial tomb within his circuit and took the buried treasure. Zhaoling was the most tightly built; it held the books of former ages and the ink of Zhong You and Wang Xizhi, the writing still fresh.

sentences.zh: （案：以下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: the text below is missing.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: the passage below is missing.)〉

sentences.zh: 移許州節度使，累官至檢校太尉、平章事。

translations.literal: He was transferred as military commissioner of Xuzhou and rose to Grand General and Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Xuzhou as military commissioner and eventually reached Grand General and Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 韜素善趙岩，每依附之。

translations.literal: Tao was always close to Zhao Yan and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had long been on good terms with Zhao Yan and constantly leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，岩恃韜與己素厚，遂奔許州。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yan relied on their old friendship and fled to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yan trusted their old ties and fled to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 韜延之於第，斬首傳送闕下。

translations.literal: Tao kept him at his mansion, then beheaded him and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tao received him in his residence, then beheaded him and sent the head to the court.

sentences.zh: 同光初，韜來朝，郭崇韜曰：「此劫陵賊，罪不可赦。

translations.literal: Early in Tongguang Tao came to court; Guo Chongtao said, "This tomb-robber's crime cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang, Tao came to court. Guo Chongtao said, "This man who plundered the imperial tombs—his crime cannot be forgiven."

sentences.zh: 」韜納賂劉後，賜姓，名紹衝，遽遣還鎮。

translations.literal: Tao bribed Empress Liu, was granted the imperial surname with the name Shaochong, and was swiftly sent back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Tao bribed Empress Liu, was granted the imperial surname and the name Shaochong, and was quickly sent back to his command.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，流於德州，俄賜死。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was exiled to Dezhou and soon ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong succeeded, Tao was exiled to Dezhou and soon ordered to die by edict.

sentences.zh: 長子延浚，清泰中為泥水關使；

translations.literal: The eldest son Yan Jun in Qingtai was barrier officer at Nishui Pass;
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yan Jun, in the Qingtai era, was officer at Nishui Pass;

sentences.zh: 次延招，為父牙帳都校；

translations.literal: the second Yan Zhao was his father's headquarters commandant;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Yan Zhao, was commandant of his father's headquarters guard;

sentences.zh: 次延袤，鄧州指揮使；

translations.literal: the third Yan Mao was commandant at Deng;
translations.idiomatic: the third, Yan Mao, was commandant at Dengzhou;

sentences.zh: 鹹聚居許下。

translations.literal: they all lived together in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and all of them dwelt together in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，聞張從賓作亂於河陽，鹹往依之。

translations.literal: Early in Jin Tianfu, hearing Zhang Congbin rebelled at Heyang, they all went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin Tianfu, when they heard that Zhang Congbin had risen at Heyang, they all went to join him.

sentences.zh: 從賓慮其難製，悉斬於帳下。

translations.literal: Congbin feared they would be hard to control and executed them all in his tent.
translations.idiomatic: Congbin feared they would be difficult to control and had them all beheaded in his tent.

sentences.zh: 段凝，開封人也。

translations.literal: Duan Ning was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 本名明遠，少穎悟，多智數。

translations.literal: His original name was Mingyuan; from youth he was clever and full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Mingyuan. Even as a youth he was quick-witted and full of schemes.

sentences.zh: 初為澠池簿，脫荷衣以事梁祖，梁祖漸器之。

translations.literal: First a clerk at Mianchi, he shed scholar's garb to serve the Liang Founder, who gradually came to value him.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk at Mianchi, then cast off his scholar's robes to serve the Liang Founder, who gradually came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 開平三年十月，自東頭供奉官授右威衛大將軍，充左軍巡使兼水北巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Kaiping he was promoted from eastern-head attendant to Right Guard General, charged as left-army patrol officer and northern-water inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kaiping year 3 he rose from eastern-head attendant to Right Guard General, and was made left-army patrol officer and northern-water inspector.

sentences.zh: 凝妹為梁祖美人，故稍委心腹。

translations.literal: Ning's sister was one of the Liang Founder's beauties, so he gained the Founder's inner trust.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's younger sister became one of the Liang Founder's palace beauties, and for that reason he won the Founder's confidential trust.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，授懷州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was made prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 4 he was appointed prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾化元年十二月，梁祖北征回，過郡，凝貢獻加等，梁祖大悅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Qianhua the Liang Founder returned north from campaign and passed through the prefecture; Ning's gifts were doubly generous and the Founder was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Qianhua year 1 the Liang Founder returned north from campaign and passed through his prefecture. Ning's tribute was richer than ever, and the Founder was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 梁祖復北，凝迎奉進貢，有加於前。

translations.literal: The Founder went north again; Ning welcomed him with gifts greater than before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder marched north again, Ning met him with gifts still more lavish than before.

sentences.zh: 梁祖次相州，刺史李思安迎奉疏怠，梁祖怒，貶思安。

translations.literal: The Founder stopped at Xiangzhou; the prefect Li Si'an's welcome was negligent and the Founder in anger demoted Si'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder halted at Xiangzhou. Prefect Li Si'an's reception was slack, and the Founder in anger demoted him.

sentences.zh: 製云：「懷州刺史段明遠，少年治郡，庶事惟公，兩度隻奉行鑾，數程宿食本界，動無遺闕，舉必周豐，蓋能罄竭於家財，務在顯酬夫明獎。

translations.literal: The edict read: "Huaizhou prefect Duan Mingyuan, though young in governing the prefecture, handles all affairs with fairness; twice he alone attended the imperial carriage, and on many stretches lodged and fed the court within his own circuit without omission, every item ample—able to exhaust his household wealth in order to show clear reward for bright merit.
translations.idiomatic: The edict declared: "Huaizhou prefect Duan Mingyuan, though young in office, governs with equity in all matters. Twice he alone attended the imperial carriage; on many stages he lodged and supplied the court within his own circuit without a single lapse, every provision complete—draining his family wealth to earn plain recognition of bright merit."

sentences.zh: 觀明遠之忠勤若此，見思安之悖慢何如！

translations.literal: Seeing Mingyuan loyal and diligent thus, compare how Si'an is insubordinate!"
translations.idiomatic: When one sees Mingyuan's loyalty and diligence on this scale, what of Si'an's insolence and neglect?"

sentences.zh: 」其見賞如此。

translations.literal: So highly he was esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 其後，遷鄭州刺史，監大軍於河上。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Zhengzhou prefect and supervised the great army on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made prefect of Zhengzhou and placed in charge of the great army on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝以戴思遠為北面招討使。

translations.literal: The Liang Last Emperor made Dai Siyuan northern campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Last Emperor appointed Dai Siyuan northern campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 行師不利，用王彥章代之，受任之翌日，取德勝之南城，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: The campaign went poorly; Wang Yanzhang replaced him. On the day after his appointment he took Desheng's south city, and army morale soared.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign fared badly, and Wang Yanzhang replaced him. The day after Yanzhang took command he seized the south city of Desheng, and the army's spirit rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 張漢倫等推功於凝，凝掎摭彥章之失以間之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hanlun and others pushed the credit onto Ning; Ning slandered Yanzhang's faults to sow discord.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hanlun and others pushed the merit onto Ning, while Ning picked at Yanzhang's faults to drive a wedge between them.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：彥章棄鄒家口，復趨楊劉。

translations.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Yanzhang abandoned Zoujiakou and rushed to Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: Yanzhang abandoned Zoujiakou and hurried to Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 遊奕將李紹興敗梁遊兵於清邱縣南，段凝以為唐兵已自上流渡，驚駭失色，麵數彥章，尤其深入。）〉

translations.literal: Patrol officer Li Shaoxing defeated Liang scouts south of Qingqiu county. Duan Ning thought Tang forces had already crossed upstream, turned pale, and scolded Yanzhang to his face, blaming him especially for advancing too deep.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Patrol officer Li Shaoxing defeated Liang scouts south of Qingqiu county. Duan Ning, believing Tang troops had already crossed upstream, turned pale and rebuked Yanzhang to his face, blaming him above all for pushing too far forward.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁末帝怒，罷彥章兵權。

translations.literal: The Liang Last Emperor was angry and stripped Yanzhang of command.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Last Emperor was enraged and removed Yanzhang's military authority.

sentences.zh: 凝納賂於趙、張二族，求為招討使，敬翔、李振極言不可，竟不能止。

translations.literal: Ning bribed the Zhao and Zhang clans to seek the post of campaign commander; Jing Xiang and Li Zhen strongly opposed it but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Ning bribed the Zhao and Zhang factions to win the post of campaign commander. Jing Xiang and Li Zhen argued strenuously against it but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 凝以眾五萬營於高陵津，裨將康延孝叛歸莊宗，延孝具陳梁軍虛實，莊宗遂決長驅之計。

translations.literal: Ning camped with fifty thousand men at Gaoling Ford; the deputy Kang Yanxiao defected to Zhuangzong and laid out the Liang army's weaknesses in full, and Zhuangzong decided on a direct march.
translations.idiomatic: Ning encamped fifty thousand men at Gaoling Ford. His deputy Kang Yanxiao defected to Zhuangzong and described the Liang forces in detail; Zhuangzong then resolved on a long thrust forward.

sentences.zh: 未幾，莊宗入汴，凝自滑率兵而南，前鋒杜晏球至封丘，解甲聽命。

translations.literal: Before long Zhuangzong entered Bian; Ning led troops south from Hua, and his vanguard Du Yanqiu at Fengqiu laid down arms and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhuangzong entered Bian. Ning marched south from Hua, while his vanguard Du Yanqiu at Fengqiu cast off his armor and submitted.

sentences.zh: 翌日，凝率大軍乞降於汴郊，莊宗釋之，復以凝為滑州兵馬留後，賜姓，名紹欽。

translations.literal: The next day Ning with the main army surrendered at the Bian suburbs; Zhuangzong pardoned him, made him military defender at Hua, and granted him the surname with the name Shaoqin.
translations.idiomatic: The following day Ning surrendered with the main force outside Bian. Zhuangzong spared him, made him military defender at Hua, and granted him the imperial surname with the name Shaoqin.

sentences.zh: 有頃，正授節度，改兗州節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly he received formal appointment as commissioner and was transferred to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received a regular commission as military commissioner and was moved to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 凝初見莊宗，因伶人景進通貨於宮掖。

translations.literal: On first meeting Zhuangzong, through the actor Jing Jin he bribed the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he first met Zhuangzong, he used the actor Jing Jin to pass gifts into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 凝天性奸佞，巧言飾智，善候人意。

translations.literal: Ning was by nature treacherous, clever in speech and false in wisdom, and skilled at reading others' wishes.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Ning was treacherous, clever with words and false in counsel, and adept at guessing what others wished to hear.

sentences.zh: 其年，契丹寇幽州，命宣徽使李紹宏監護諸軍，以禦契丹，凝與董璋戍瓦橋關。

translations.literal: That year the Khitan raided Youzhou; Li Shaohong was made palace commissioner to supervise the armies against the Khitan, and Ning with Dong Zhang held Waqiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Khitan attacked Youzhou. Li Shaohong was sent as palace commissioner to oversee the armies against them, while Ning and Dong Zhang guarded Waqiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 凝巧事紹宏，紹宏嘗乘間奏凝蓋世奇才，可以大任，屢請以兵柄委之。

translations.literal: Ning curried favor with Shaohong; Shaohong several times memorialized that Ning was a matchless talent fit for great trust and repeatedly asked that military power be entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ning fawned on Shaohong, who in turn several times memorialized that Ning was a talent without peer and fit for heavy responsibility, repeatedly asking that the command of troops be given to him.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜曰：「段凝亡國敗軍之將，奸諂難狀，不要信也。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao said, "Duan Ning is the general who lost the state and army; his treachery is hard to describe—do not trust him."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao said, "Duan Ning is the commander who lost the state and the army. His flattery is beyond description—do not trust him."

sentences.zh: 」凝在藩鎮，私用庫物數萬計，有司促償，中旨貰其負。

translations.literal: At his fief he privately used treasury goods worth tens of thousands; the authorities pressed for repayment, but an imperial edict remitted his debt.
translations.idiomatic: While holding a command he privately drew on treasury goods worth tens of thousands. The relevant offices demanded repayment, but an imperial edict canceled what he owed.

sentences.zh: 同光三年四月，移授鄧州節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Tongguang he was transferred to Dengzhou as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tongguang year 3 he was transferred to Dengzhou as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，趙在禮據鄴城，李紹宏請用凝為大將，莊宗許之，令具方略條奏。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili held Yecheng; Li Shaohong asked that Ning be made great general; Zhuangzong agreed and ordered a plan set out in items.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 4 Zhao Zaili seized Yecheng. Li Shaohong asked that Ning be made supreme commander. Zhuangzong agreed and ordered him to submit a detailed plan.

sentences.zh: 凝所請偏裨皆取其己黨，莊宗疑之，乃止。

translations.literal: All the deputies Ning requested were men of his own faction; Zhuangzong grew suspicious and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Every deputy Ning named was from his own clique. Zhuangzong grew suspicious and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 明宗至洛陽，霍彥威怒其前事，與溫韜同收下獄，詔釋之，放歸田里。

translations.literal: When Mingzong reached Luoyang, Huo Yanwei was angry over his past conduct; he and Wen Tao were arrested together, then an edict released them and sent them back to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong came to Luoyang, Huo Yanwei was incensed over his earlier conduct. He and Wen Tao were seized and imprisoned together, then an edict released them and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 明年，竄於遼州，竟與溫韜同製賜死。

translations.literal: The next year he fled to Liaozhou and in the end was ordered to die by the same edict as Wen Tao.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he fled to Liaozhou and was finally ordered to die under the same edict as Wen Tao.

sentences.zh: 孔謙，

translations.literal: Kong Qian,
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》作魏州人。）〉

translations.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror gives his native place as Weizhou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Comprehensive Mirror says he was a man of Weizhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 莊宗同光初，為租庸副使。

translations.literal: Early in Tongguang Zhuangzong made him deputy commissioner for tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang, Zhuangzong appointed him deputy commissioner for tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 謙本州之幹吏，上自天祐十二年，帝平定魏博，會計皆委製置。

translations.literal: Qian was originally a capable clerk of the prefecture; from the twelfth year of Tianyou onward, when the Emperor pacified Weibo, all accounting was entrusted to his management.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had been a capable clerk in the prefecture. From Tianyou year 12, when the Emperor pacified Weibo, all fiscal accounts were placed in his hands.

sentences.zh: 謙能曲事權要，效其才力，帝委以泉貨之務，設法箕斂，七八年間，軍儲獲濟。

translations.literal: Qian could bend to serve the powerful and exert his abilities; the Emperor entrusted him with money affairs, devised methods of heavy levying, and within seven or eight years army stores were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Qian knew how to curry favor with the powerful and put his talents to use. The Emperor entrusted him with fiscal affairs; he devised schemes of squeezing levies, and within seven or eight years the army's stores were kept full.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位於鄴城，謙已當為租庸使。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne at Yecheng, Qian ought already to have become commissioner for tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Emperor took the throne at Yecheng, Qian was already the natural choice for commissioner of tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 物議以謙雖有經營濟贍之勞，然人地尚卑，不欲驟總重任。

translations.literal: Public opinion held that although Qian had merit in managing and supplying funds, his person and standing were still low, and people did not wish to place great responsibility on him all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that although Qian had merit in managing and supplying the treasury, his rank and standing were still low, and courtiers did not want to thrust the highest office on him at once.

sentences.zh: 樞密使郭崇韜舉魏博觀察判官張憲為租庸使，以謙為副，謙悒然不樂者久之。

translations.literal: Military Affairs Commissioner Guo Chongtao recommended Zhang Xian, observation judge of Weibo, as commissioner for tax and corvée, with Qian as deputy; Qian was displeased for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao, Military Affairs Commissioner, recommended Zhang Xian, observation judge at Weibo, as commissioner, with Qian as deputy. Qian brooded over this for a long time.

sentences.zh: 帝既平梁汴，謙徑自魏州馳之行在，因謂崇韜曰：「魏都重地，須大臣彈壓，以謙籌之，非張憲不可。

translations.literal: After the Emperor had pacified Liang Bian, Qian rode straight from Weizhou to the imperial camp and said to Chongtao: "Yecheng is a vital place and requires a great minister to hold it down; in Qian's reckoning Zhang Xian cannot do it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Emperor had pacified the Liang capital at Bian, Qian galloped from Weizhou to the imperial camp and told Chongtao: "Yecheng is a vital post and needs a senior minister to keep it firm. By my judgment Zhang Xian is not the man."

sentences.zh: 」崇韜以為忠告，即奏憲為鄴都副留守，乃命宰臣豆盧革專判租庸。

translations.literal: " Chongtao took this as sincere counsel and at once memorialized that Zhang Xian should be deputy garrison commandant of Yecheng; the chief minister Dou Lüge was then ordered to handle tax and corvée affairs alone.
translations.idiomatic: " Chongtao took this as honest advice and immediately memorialized Zhang Xian as deputy garrison commandant of Yecheng, while chief minister Dou Lüge alone was put in charge of tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 謙彌失望，乃尋革過失。

translations.literal: Qian was still more disappointed and then sought out Lüge's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Qian grew still more bitter and began hunting for Lüge's mistakes.

sentences.zh: 時革以手書便省庫錢數十萬，謙以手書示崇韜，亦辭避。

translations.literal: At the time Lüge had by personal letter drawn several hundred thousand from the convenience treasury; Qian showed the letter to Chongtao, who also declined the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lüge had taken several hundred thousand from the convenience treasury by personal letter. Qian showed the letter to Chongtao, who likewise refused the assignment.

sentences.zh: 帝問：「當委何人為可？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked: "Whom should be entrusted with this?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "Who should take the post?"

sentences.zh: 」崇韜曰：「孔謙雖久掌貨泉，然物議未當居大任，以臣所見，當委張憲為便。

translations.literal: " Chongtao said: "Although Qian has long managed money affairs, public opinion does not deem him fit for a great post; in my view Zhang Xian would be suitable."
translations.idiomatic: " Chongtao replied, "Qian has long handled money affairs, but opinion does not yet deem him fit for the top post. In my view Zhang Xian would be the better choice."

sentences.zh: 」帝促征之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor urgently summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor hurriedly summoned Zhang Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲性精辨，為趨時者所忌，人不祐之。

translations.literal: Zhang was by nature sharp and discriminating; the time-servers resented him and no one supported him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was sharp and discriminating by nature. Men who chased fashion resented him, and no one spoke up for him.

sentences.zh: 謙乘間訴於豆盧革曰：「租庸錢穀，悉在眼前，委一小吏可辦。

translations.literal: Qian seized an opening to complain to Dou Lüge: "The money and grain of tax and corvée are all before one's eyes; entrusting it to a petty clerk would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Qian seized a chance to complain to Dou Lüge: "Tax and corvée funds are plain to see; a minor clerk could manage them."

sentences.zh: 鄴都本根之地，不可輕付於人。

translations.literal: Yecheng is the root of the state and must not be lightly entrusted to another.
translations.idiomatic: Yecheng is the foundation of the realm and must not be lightly handed to anyone.

sentences.zh: 興唐尹王正言無裨益之才，徒有獨行，詔書既征張憲，復以何人為代？

translations.literal: Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan has no talent for real benefit, only a reputation for upright conduct. Now that an edict has summoned Zhang Xian, who should replace him?"
translations.idiomatic: Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan has no talent that truly helps the state, only a reputation for solitary integrity. The edict has already summoned Zhang Xian—who should take his place?"

sentences.zh: 」豆盧革言於崇韜，崇韜曰：「鄴都分司列職，皆主上舊人，委王正言何慮不辦？

translations.literal: " Lüge spoke to Chongtao, and Chongtao said: "The branch offices and ranks at Yecheng are all the sovereign's old followers; entrusting Wang Zhengyan—what worry is there that it cannot be done?"
translations.idiomatic: " Lüge spoke to Chongtao, who said, "The branch offices at Yecheng are staffed with the sovereign's old men. If Wang Zhengyan is entrusted with it, what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」革曰：「俱是失也，設不獲已，以正言掌租庸，取書於大臣，或可辦矣；

translations.literal: " Lüge said: "Both choices are wrong. If there is no help for it, let Zhengyan manage tax and corvée and take written instructions from the great ministers—perhaps that can be done;
translations.idiomatic: " Lüge said, "Both courses are mistakes. If we must choose, let Zhengyan handle tax and corvée and take written instructions from the senior ministers—perhaps that could work;

sentences.zh: 若付之方面，必敗人事。

translations.literal: if entrusted to a frontier commissioner, affairs will surely be ruined."
translations.idiomatic: but if it is given to a frontier commissioner, affairs will surely be ruined."

sentences.zh: 」謙以正言非德非勳，懦而易製，曰：「此議為便。

translations.literal: " Qian, because Zhengyan lacked virtue and merit and was timid and easy to control, said: "This plan is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: " Qian, seeing that Zhengyan lacked virtue and merit and was timid and easy to manipulate, said, "That plan will do."

sentences.zh: 」然非己誌。

translations.literal: " Yet it was not his own wish.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet it was not what he truly wanted.

sentences.zh: 尋掎正言之失，泣訴於崇韜，厚賂閹伶，以求進用，人知奸諂，沮之，乃上章請退。

translations.literal: Before long he picked at Zhengyan's faults, wept and appealed to Chongtao, bribed eunuch actors heavily to seek advancement; when people knew his flattery and treachery and blocked him, he submitted a memorial asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he seized on Zhengyan's faults, wept before Chongtao, and lavished bribes on eunuch actors to win promotion. When men saw his flattery and blocked him, he submitted a memorial asking to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其規避，將置於法，樂人景進於帝前解喻而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry at his evasion and was about to punish him by law; the musician Jing Jin explained before the Emperor and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angry at his shirking and was about to punish him. The musician Jing Jin pleaded before the throne and stayed the matter.

sentences.zh: 王正言風病恍惚，不能綜三司事，景進屢言於帝，乃以正言守禮部尚書，以謙為租庸使。

translations.literal: Wang Zhengyan suffered from wind sickness and mental confusion and could not oversee the Three Departments; Jing Jin spoke repeatedly to the Emperor, and Zhengyan was made Minister of Rites while Qian became commissioner for tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengyan was afflicted with wind sickness and mental confusion and could not manage the Three Departments. Jing Jin spoke to the Emperor again and again, until Zhengyan was made Minister of Rites and Qian became commissioner for tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 謙以國用不足，奏：「諸道判官員數過多，請隻置節度、觀察、判官、書記、支使、推官各一員。

translations.literal: Qian, because state revenue was insufficient, memorialized: "The number of circuit judges in the various circuits is excessive; please set only one each for military commissioner, observation commissioner, judge, secretary, branch commissioner, and investigating officer."
translations.idiomatic: Because state revenue was insufficient, Qian memorialized: "There are too many circuit judges in the provinces. Please allow only one each for military commissioner, observation commissioner, judge, secretary, branch commissioner, and investigating officer."

sentences.zh: 留守置判官各一員。

translations.literal: For garrison commandants, one judge each.
translations.idiomatic: For garrison commandants, one judge each.

sentences.zh: 三京府置判官、推官，餘並罷俸錢。

translations.literal: For the three capital prefectures, judges and investigating officers; all others' salary payments should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For the three capital prefectures, judges and investigating officers; all other salary payments should be cut off.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「百官俸錢雖多，折支非實，請減半數，皆支實錢。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Although officials' salaries are large in nominal terms, the discounted payments are not real; please cut them by half and pay all in real cash."
translations.idiomatic: " He also memorialized: "Although officials' salaries are large on paper, the discounted payments are not real money. Please cut them by half and pay entirely in cash."

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: " Both were approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，半年俸復從虛折。

translations.literal: Before long, within half a year salaries again followed fictitious discount.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, within half a year salaries again followed fictitious discount payments.

sentences.zh: （案：以下原闕。

translations.literal: (Note: the original text below is missing.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: the original passage below is missing.

sentences.zh: 《北夢瑣言》：明宗即位，誅租庸使孔謙等。

translations.literal: Idle Words of Northern Dreams: When Mingzong took the throne he executed the commissioner for tax and corvée Kong Qian and others.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Dreams, Idle Words: When Mingzong succeeded, he executed Kong Qian, commissioner for tax and corvée, and others.

sentences.zh: 孔謙者，魏州孔目。

translations.literal: Kong Qian was a clerk of accounts at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian had been a fiscal clerk at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗圖霸，以供饋兵食，謙有力焉。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong plotted for hegemony, Qian supplied army provisions and had great force in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong was fighting for supremacy, Qian helped supply the army's food and played a major part.

sentences.zh: 既為租庸使，曲事嬖幸，奪宰相權，專以聚斂為意，剝削為端。

translations.literal: Once he became commissioner for tax and corvée, he curried favor with the emperor's favorites, seized power from the chancellors, and devoted himself wholly to amassing wealth, making exploitation his starting point.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became commissioner, he fawned on the emperor's favorites, stripped power from the chancellors, and devoted himself wholly to amassing wealth, taking exploitation as his trade.

sentences.zh: 以犯眾怒，伏誅。）〉

translations.literal: Because he aroused public wrath he was executed.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He aroused universal anger and was put to death.)〉

sentences.zh: 李鄴，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Li Ye was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye came from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼事楊師厚，及莊宗入魏，漸轉裨將，曆數郡刺史，後遷亳州。

translations.literal: In youth he served Yang Shihou; when Zhuangzong entered Wei he gradually rose to deputy general, served as prefect of several prefectures, and was later transferred to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served Yang Shihou. When Zhuangzong entered Wei he rose by degrees to deputy general, held several prefectures in succession, and was later moved to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 為政貪穢，有奴為人持金以賂鄴，奴隱其金，鄴殺之。

translations.literal: His government was greedy and filthy; a slave held gold on another's behalf to bribe Ye, but the slave hid the gold and Ye killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was greedy and corrupt. A slave was carrying gold for someone else to bribe Ye; the slave concealed the gold, and Ye killed him.

sentences.zh: 其家上訴，因訐其陰事，詔貶郴州司戶參軍，又貶崖州長流百姓，所在賜自盡。

translations.literal: His family appealed upward; because they denounced his secret affairs, an edict demoted him to registrar at Chenzhou, then exiled him as commoner to Yazhou with orders to grant self-death wherever he was.
translations.idiomatic: The family appealed. Because they exposed his hidden conduct, an edict demoted him to registrar at Chenzhou, then exiled him as a commoner to Yazhou with orders that wherever he was found he should be allowed to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：《易》云：「積不善之家，必有餘殃。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Book of Changes states: "A house that accumulates evil will surely have surplus calamity."
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: The Book of Changes says, "A house that accumulates evil will surely have calamity left over."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「惡不積不足以滅身。

translations.literal: " It also says: "Evil that is not accumulated is insufficient to destroy the person."
translations.idiomatic: " It also says, "Evil that is not accumulated is not enough to destroy the person."

sentences.zh: 」如毛璋之儔，可謂積惡而滅其身矣，況溫韜之發陵寢，段凝之敗國家，罪不容誅，死猶差晚。

translations.literal: " Men like Mao Zhang may be said to have accumulated evil until it destroyed them; how much more Wen Tao, who opened imperial tombs, and Duan Ning, who ruined the state—their crimes could not be pardoned, and even death came late.
translations.idiomatic: " Men like Mao Zhang may be said to have piled up evil until it destroyed them. How much more Wen Tao, who opened imperial tombs, and Duan Ning, who ruined the state—their crimes could not be forgiven, and even death came late.

sentences.zh: 餘皆瑣瑣，何足議焉。

translations.literal: The rest were petty matters and not worth discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were trifles and hardly merit discussion.
